_meta.purpose: Cited provenance for every boundary in config/regions.geojson. Sidecar by design: config/regions.geojson is a LOFRA-sealed artifact and is NEVER edited to carry this metadata, so its byte identity (and every derived mask/state/forecast hash) is preserved. Human narrative lives in docs/region_provenance.md; the machine-checkable `checks` here are enforced by tests/test_region_provenance.py so accidental boundary drift fails CI.
_meta.doctrine: This is an ESR ecosystem board. The AUTHORITATIVE boundary reference is the AFSC ESR ECOREGIONS, not the fishery-management statistical/survey areas (NMFS 541/542/543). The two systems overlap and disagree by design. Canonical example: the AI Central<->East divide is the ESR ecoregion break at Samalga Pass (~170°W), NOT the management district break at 177°W.
_meta.measured_frame: checks use signed lon in [-180,180) for lon_min/lon_max, lon in [0,360) for lon_min_360/lon_max_360 (dateline-crossing AI), and degrees N for lat_min/lat_max, all read from the polygon vertices.

provenance.quote: The Central Aleutian Islands ecoregion spans 177°E to 170°W. ... the eastern boundary of this ecoregion occurs at Samalga Pass, which is at 169.5°W, but for easier translation to fishery management area, it was agreed that 170°W was a close approximation.
The Eastern Aleutian Islands ecoregion spans 170°W to False Pass at 164°W. ... This area encompasses the NPFMC fishery management areas 518, 519 (EBS) and the western half of 610 (GOA).
